title: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence
key_facts: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon, a new frontier model, on 8 Oct 2026.
It is rolling out first to a set of trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program; these users and Google's own teams get it without cyber guardrails.
Wider release to developers, enterprises and consumers comes later, starting with paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers; no date given.
Google says it is in the US government's voluntary process for pre-release model access.
Introductory price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens; $4 and $20 after the introductory period.
Output limit rises to 1M tokens, up from 64K.
Google's own benchmark claims: 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1, first on the Vals Index, 51.3% (rank 1) on Zapier's AutomationBench, 91.7% on LVBench, 68% (tied first) on CWE-bench v1.
Google says Argon can autonomously find, validate and patch critical software vulnerabilities; Wiz used it to find a critical flaw in healthcare software used by hospitals.
quote_evidence: Today, we’re announcing our new frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, which is rolling out to a set of trusted cyber defenders through our Fairwind Program.
We are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model access while we gradually expand access.
It sets a new state of the art on DeepSWE v1.1 (77.9%), which measures a model’s performance in real-world long-horizon software engineering tasks.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading AI lab is releasing its strongest model first to security defenders, without its usual cyber safeguards, before a wider launch.
notes: All benchmark results are Google's own. Pool marks this a follow-up of 6 Oct pool item C01-05 (OfficeChai: Argon with Antigravity placed ahead of GPT 6.1 Sol on a coding-agent index, 5 Oct); the official launch is new today.
